Where It Begins

Rooted in
Kenyan Highlands

Kenya produces some of the world's most prized coffee — grown at elevations above 1,800 metres, where cool nights and volcanic soils impart a brightness and complexity unmatched anywhere else on earth.

Mokal Coffee sources exclusively from small-holder farms in the Central Highlands, working directly with growers to ensure quality from cherry to cup and fair returns for every harvest.

Fast Start Guide

Brew It
Right

Great coffee begins with great technique. Follow our recommended methods to unlock the full spectrum of flavour that Kenyan Arabica has to offer.

Two tablespoons per 200ml is our golden ratio — adjust to taste as you discover your perfect cup.

Pro Tip

Store in a cool, dry place. Once opened, preferably refrigerate to preserve freshness and flavour integrity.

Plunger Method
01Add 2 level tablespoons of ground coffee per 200ml.
02Use freshly boiled water — not boiling. Let it rest 30 seconds off the heat.
03Allow to infuse for 4–5 minutes before pressing the plunger.
04Serve immediately for peak flavour.
Filter Method
01Start with fresh, cold water for the best extraction.
02Measure 2 level tablespoons of ground coffee per 200ml.
03Adjust grind coarseness to your machine's guidelines.
04Follow your machine manufacturer's instructions for timing.

"Coffee is a language in itself — and Kenya speaks it with a richness, a brightness, and a depth that the world is only beginning to truly understand."

— Mokal Coffee, Nairobi

Our Story

A Passion for
Kenyan Coffee

Mokal Coffee was born from a simple belief: that Kenya's extraordinary coffee deserved to be roasted, packaged, and shared with the world — by Kenyans, on their own terms.

We work hand-in-hand with smallholder farmers across the Central Highlands, paying premium prices for exceptional cherries and roasting each batch to bring out the unique character of every farm's terroir.

From our base in Nairobi, we ship across Kenya and beyond — because the world deserves to know what real Kenyan coffee tastes like, brewed with love and roasted with purpose.

East Africa

East African coffees are celebrated worldwide for their extraordinary brightness, wine-like complexity, and vibrant fruit-forward profiles. Grown at elevations above 1,500 metres on volcanic soils, these coffees consistently deliver an experience unlike any other origin.

Kenya produces legendary SL28 and SL34 varietals with blackcurrant and tomato-juice complexity. Tanzania's slopes of Kilimanjaro and Mbeya yield structured, chocolate-tinged cups. Burundi's Bourbon varieties from Kayanza and Ngozi offer stone-fruit sweetness with a silky, tea-like finish.

Home · Green Coffee · African

East Africa

East African coffees are celebrated for extraordinary complexity and vibrancy. Kenya's volcanic highlands yield bright, wine-like acidity with blackcurrant and citrus clarity. Uganda's Mt. Elgon farms produce clean, full-bodied cups with deep chocolate and floral notes. Tanzania's rich soils deliver stone-fruit depth, while Burundi's bourbon varietals offer floral, tea-like finesse.

Sourced directly from smallholder farms across the East African Rift Valley — traceable, ethical, and rooted in generations of growing tradition.
